newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Jan 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Jan 26.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
SUNDAY TELEGRAPH
-- WALL ST BANK TO TAKE OVER PHOENIX

Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette, the US investment bank, is set to acquire Phoenix Securities in a deal worth 50 million pounds stg. Phoenix will be the latest corporate finance house sold for top dollar and will give DLJ a desired increased presence in London.
-- GEC TO SELL CREDA AND HOTPOINT

General Electric Company is in talks with leading venture-capital groups about the disposal of its consumer electronics business, including Creda cookers and Hotpoint washing machines. The disposal is expected to value GEC's stake at 150 million pounds stg, and follows the group's announcement last week of plans to restructure its operations.
-- SAINSBURY HITS PLANNING SNAG

J Sainsbury is backing a threat of legal action against the government following a planning error by civil servants that caused the construction of its flagship superstore in Northern Ireland to be halted. A letter has been sent to the government stating that legal action will be taken to recover losses if planning consent is not renewed promptly.
-- BA TO DISPOSE OF CATERING ARM

British Airways is set to sell its long-haul intercontinental catering operations based at Heathrow. Talks are at an early stage, with likely purchasers being Gate Gourmet, Dobbs and LSG Skychef. The business employs 1,100 and produces more than 120,000 in-flight meals a week.
-- C&W PONDERS PANAMA STAKE

Cable & Wireless is looking at the possibility of making a bid for 49 percent of Intel, Panama's state owned telecommunications business. Intel is thought to be worth around 2 billion dollars US. Cable and Wireless was given the go-ahead to make a bid in December and has until March 31 to make an offer.
SUNDAY TIMES
-- BRITISH GAS MAY ESCAPE TOUGH OFGAS PRICE CUTS

Plans by Ofgas to cut the prices charged by TransCo, British Gas's pipeline operation, may not get backing from the Monopolies Mergers Commission. The MMC may water down the proposals from the gas industry watchdog to cut prices by 20 percent.
-- LEADING GE EXECUTIVE BACKS BLAIR

Christopher Mackenzie, president of GE Capital Europe has publicly pledged his personal support for the Labour party. After a meeting with Tony Blair on Thursday, Mackenzie said the Labour leader had persuaded him that Labour offered business a better choice than the present government.
-- BIOTECH FIRM SET FOR 85 MILLION POUNDS FLOAT

Cambridge Antibody Technology, the biotechnology company, will announce its intention to float this week. Sponsored by Kleinwort Benson and Cazenove, the listing will value the company at 85-100 million pounds stg.
-- VOSPER SET TO LAND GULF DEAL

Southampton-based shipbuilder Vosper Thornycroft is near to winning a 700 million pounds stg order from the United Arab Emirates, according to industry insiders. Vosper is also pitching to win a massive 27-ship deal with Malaysia with a headline value of 2 billion pounds stg.
-- LONDON CROWNED BY LOUIS VUITTON

Louis Vuitton, the luxury French luggage company, has picked London rather than Paris for its new flagship store. The move strengthens London's claim to be the European centre of fashion. The 12,000 sq ft store will be located in New Bond Street and will open in the summer.
THE OBSERVER
-- ABN SAW KEY ROLE FOR OUSTED MORGAN BOSS

According to affidavits gathered by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Keith Percy, who was ousted from the company following the Peter Young scandal, was to have worked alongside Nicola Horlick at the head of a fund management business planned by ABN Amro. Horlick was suspended from Morgan Grenfell two weeks ago accused of plotting to help ABN poach staff.
-- UTILITY TAX CHANGES "WILL PUSH UP BILLS"

If the Government goes ahead with its plans for a version of a windfall tax on utilities, electricity and water bills will go up. The warning came in a strongly worded letter from the Electricity Association to Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, stating that new tax measures announced in the Budget would lead to an increase in prices.
-- OPEN-SIDED SHUTTLE WAGONS PUT ON HOLD

Eurotunnel is delaying the production of new open-sided wagons for its freight shuttle while it agrees new safety procedures for carrying lorries. The 14 million pounds stg worth of additional wagons ordered from Arbel, the French manufacturer, offer lorries less protection than the present lattice-sided shuttles.
-- CHELSFIELD BOSS TO BUY GRANADA HOTELS FOR 80 MILLION POUNDS

Elliott Bernerd, the head of Chelsfield, the property group, is set to buy Granada's two Westbury hotels for 80 million pounds stg. The two sides are presently sorting out legal difficulties, but the deal for the Westbury, Mayfair, and the Westbury, New York, should be completed this week, before Granada's AGM.
-- RANK LOOKING TO HAVE A FLUTTER ON AMERICAN CASINOS

The Rank Corporation is looking for a deal with a US casino company to develop an American gaming operation. The leisure giant is talking with several US companies about a joint casino venture, possibly linked with the Hard Rock Cafe.
INDEPENDENT ON SUNDAY
-- HOUSE OF FRASER CUTS 1,000 JOBS

House of Fraser is to announce around 1,000 job cuts tomorrow as part of a sweeping store closure programme. The group, which includes the Army & Navy and Dickins & Jones department stores, is expected to close at least six of its 52 stores.
-- TERMINAL 5 PUT IN JEOPARDY

The future of Heathrow airport's Terminal 5 project has been put into doubt following last week's announcement by Boeing that it is shelving plans to build a super-jumbo. The proposed terminal relies heavily in its design on the presence of such large commercial aircraft.
-- TAXMAN ON THE TRAIL OF HINCHLIFFE

Inspectors from the Inland Revenue are understood to be examining the affairs of businessman Stephen Hinchliffe, in the latest turn in the saga of his failed Facia retail business. Already under investigation by the Serious Fraud Office, the new investigation focuses on alleged corruption at Israel's United Mizrahi Bank over loans to Facia.
-- SEARS MOVE HINTS AT BSC SELL-OFF

Sears, the retail group, is dropping plans to create a single distribution centre because of the uncertainty over the future of its British Shoe corporation subsidiary. The move is the clearest sign yet that the company is preparing to sell BSC in the coming months.
-- GULF SET TO QUIT FIGHT FOR CLYDE

Gulf Canada is believed to be pulling out of its battle to take over Clyde Petroleum following the receipt of acceptances from only 1 percent of the shareholders. Institutional shareholders in Clyde demanded a revised offer of around 135p per share well above Gulf's offer of 105p.
MAIL ON SUNDAY
-- PRU MAY BID 1.5 BILLION POUNDS IN SCOTAM SWOOP

Prudential, the insurance giant, is looking at making a 1.5 billion pounds stg bid for Scottish Amicable. An offer may be announced in the coming few weeks, before ScotAm launches its own two-stage process to become a quoted company.
-- ESSO FACES REVOLT ON THE FORECOURT

Esso service station operators are threatening to rebel over the way the oil company has raised rents to levels that wipe out their profits. The Esso Licensed Retailers Association believes the terms of trade are illegal and has formally complained to the European Commission.
-- VAT BLOW CURBS THE DEVELOPERS

Moves to impose VAT on building works for banks and insurance companies announced in the last budget, is slowing speculative property development. Many top developers have been force to put plans on hold as costs rise by up to 20 percent.
-- MIDLAND BACKS CRITICS OF BA DEAL

The chairman of British Midland is to tell the European commission that British Airways' must give up some take-off and landing rights from Heathrow Airport to cities on the Continent. This comes as another blow to BAs' planned alliance with American Airlines, having already agreed to give up 168 slots on services to America.
-- SAUDI SET TO BUY BAe AIRCRAFT

British Aerospace is expected to announce an order from the Saudi Arabia state airline, Saudia, next month. The 160 million pounds stg contract for 12 jets will be placed with Avro, BAe's small aircraft division.
